a1.say: Let's build Safe Money Transfer With at Transactional.

a1.cap: Implement transfer(fromId, toId, amount) so both balance updates succeed or neither does, insufficient funds are rejected, and two concurrent transfers can't silently overwrite each other's updates.
a1.say: Implement transfer(from Id, to Id, amount) so both balance updates succeed or neither does, insufficient funds are rejected, and two concurrent transfers can't silently overwrite each other's updates.

lines: Implement transfer(fromId, toId, amount) so both balance updates succeed or neither does, insufficient funds are rejected, and two concurrent transfers can't silently overwrite each other's updates.

a1.cap: @Transactional wraps the method in one database transaction: if anything throws, both updates roll back. Inside it, JPA's dirty checking writes the changed balances automatically on commit.
a1.say: at Transactional wraps the method in one database transaction: if anything throws, both updates roll back. Inside it, JPA's dirty checking writes the changed balances automatically on commit.

a1.cap: The @Version column makes concurrent updates safe: if another transaction changed the row first, the commit fails with an optimistic-lock exception instead of losing an update.
a1.say: The at Version column makes concurrent updates safe: if another transaction changed the row first, the commit fails with an optimistic-lock exception instead of losing an update.

a1.cap: Money uses BigDecimal, never double, to avoid rounding errors.
